sentences: The Anti-Breakthrough (Micro-Dosing): A brain stuck in alarm can often take in healing work for only a few seconds at a time, Perry finds.
So for now we have to give up on the hour-long breakthrough that therapy aims for, since an hour spent working on the trauma itself overwhelms an armored nervous system more than it heals it.
Instead, this protocol works in doses of a few seconds, which is what I mean by micro-dosing here.
So your goal is 30 seconds of slow and steady breathing, twenty times a day, since short sessions done often help an armored nervous system more than one long session does.

sonnet: The paragraph is built as claim, then reason, then claim, then reason, and nearly every sentence ends in a "since..." or "more than..." clause. The rhythm is even and the sentences are about the same length, and every idea gets an explanation. The voice stays neutral and instructional, with no tangents, asides or uneven moments.
